html:
Mindaugas was the first known ruler of all Lithuania and its only crowned king. He was crowned on 6 July 1253, now Lithuania's Statehood Day.

He united the Lithuanian tribes in the 1230s and 1240s by war, marriage and murder. Threatened by the Livonian Order, he accepted baptism in 1251 and a crown from the pope, and gave land to the knights.

About ten years later he broke with them and probably returned to the old gods. In 1263 he was murdered by rivals. His kingdom did not last, but the state he built grew into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Gediminas. Lithuania itself was only finally baptised in 1387. See Lithuania.
sum: Mindaugas was the first known ruler of all Lithuania and its only crowned king. He was crowned on 6 July 1253, now Lithuania's Statehood Day.
